result.title: Do vision models know that three is three?
result.summary: Do vision models encode the transition $2{\to}3$ the same way whether it appears in handwritten digits or in hand gestures, and do they "understand" that clean${\to}$dirty is the same transformation regardless of whether it is applied to a kitchen or a carpet? The linear representation hypothesis (LRH) answers this for language models: concept changes correspond to directions in (language) embedding space. In vision, the same concept can manifest in visually unrelated "regimes" that rarely co-occur: images of digits and hands do not share much in common in pixel space. To understand whether vision models still encode the underlying abstract concepts, we study 46 vision encoders across architectures, training objectives, and scales, on 10 concept families including numerosity, age, object identity, and MIT-States attributes. Within each regime, we find statistically significant concept directions near-universally across our tested models. However, two distinct regimes do not always share the same concept direction. Several models learn multiple linear structures for the same concept transition, split across regimes. We call this phenomenon "fragmented linearity": strong local linearity coexisting with near-absent global linearity. Fragmentation is, however, not fixed: models with stronger local linearity progressively escape it (local-global linearity correlated with $τ\in [0.38, 0.89]$ across all concepts), and where global linearity does emerge, concept directions can transfer as linear probes across regimes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在46个视觉编码器上检验线性表示假设：同一抽象概念变化（数量、年龄、物体身份、MIT-States属性等10类）在不同视觉「regime」（如手写数字与手势）中是否对应同一方向，发现局部线性近乎普遍、跨regime的全局线性常缺失，称之为「fragmented linearity」，且局部线性越强的模型越能逐步转向全局线性并使概念方向可作线性探针迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉编码器内部状态是否保留可迁移的抽象概念信息，为判断LVR中视觉旁路是否丢失任务必要内容提供诊断线索；但研究的是静态特征线性结构而非推理期状态生成，与latent推理的联系需核查。
